reviewedFrom: B14.1/B14.2 definitions of done (advisor-plans/013) and docs/books-entities.md.

payment-across-companies.derivation: The builder (primary company) owns the job; the land company owns checking account 1005. A $30,000 bill on the job is the builder's (Dr 5000 / Cr 2000). Paying it from the land company's checking: the builder's side is Dr 2000, the land company's is Cr 1005, and posting adds the builder's Cr 2180 due to the land company and the land company's Dr 1180 due from the builder, so each balances on its own. Consolidated, the 1180/2180 pair is eliminated: the group spent $30,000 of cash on job cost. Each company files its own 1099s: the $30,000 check came from the land company's checking, so it is the land company's 1099 payment to the framing sub, and not the builder's.

ownership-fixed-and-reversal.derivation: Once the job and the land company's account have postings, moving either to another company is refused. Voiding the check posts Dr 1005 (land) / Cr 2000 (builder); the land company now owes the builder, which first settles what the builder owed it: Cr 1180 on the land company and Dr 2180 on the builder. Afterwards the land company has nothing (cash back, nothing owed) and the builder has its job cost and the bill owed again; neither carries a receivable and a payable with the other.

single-company-unchanged.derivation: A builder with one company has its primary company created on first posting; every line is on it, no intercompany account is created, no company choice is offered, and its consolidated statements are its company's statements.

company-subledgers-and-close.derivation: The builder's contract job is invoiced $50,000 and billed $30,000; the land company's lot-sale job (purchase agreement, earned at invoicing) is invoiced $20,000 and billed $8,000. Each company's receivables and payables aging equals its own 1100 and 2000. July then closes (the land company's idle checking reconciled at zero): the close saves the 8 consolidated reports plus trial balance, P&L, balance sheet, cash flow, AR and AP aging for each company. The land company's July statements and aging then read as closed; its net income is $20,000 − $8,000 = $12,000.

intercompany-lot-sale.derivation: The land company (owner of land account 1120 and checking 1005) buys lot 9 for $60,000 and sells it to the builder's home for $75,000: land company revenue $75,000, cost $60,000, due from the builder $75,000; the builder's home takes the lot in at $75,000 and owes the land company. A sale without a price is refused. The builder adds $200,000 of construction and completes the home ($275,000 in 1170). Consolidated before the outside sale: the land company's sale and the due-from/due-to are eliminated and the home stands at $260,000 — the lot at its $60,000 cost. The home then sells for $300,000: land company profit $15,000, builder profit $300,000 − $275,000 = $25,000, group profit $40,000 = $300,000 − $260,000, exactly the two companies' profits. The reconciliation pair ties at $75,000 and the lot sale's $15,000 profit is realized. The close's intercompany control passes: every company's due-from agrees with its affiliate's due-to.

expected.priceRequired: refused: a sale price is required

company-openings.derivation: The land company opens with $10,000 of prepaid insurance against owner equity, posted as its own batch; the builder (primary company) opens with $5,000. A land-company batch whose prepaid line sits on the builder's job resolves to two companies and is refused. Each company's trial balance at cutover is exactly its own position; consolidated is their sum, with nothing owed between them.

expected.mixed: refused: lines belong to more than one company

archive-round-trip.derivation: The builder's $30,000 bill paid from the land company's checking leaves the land company owed $30,000. Inside one rolled-back transaction every exported row of the organization is deleted and reinserted from the export snapshot alone: each company's balance by account and the intercompany positions are identical. On the restored data a new $1,000 builder cost paid from the land company's checking gets its two legs (the land company is then owed $31,000), and moving the job to another company is still refused. The export bundle itself verifies.

foreign-company-refused.derivation: A company belongs to one organization. Another organization naming it is refused when assigning a job, opening its books or posting a line (the line's company must be in the line's organization), and a statement asked for it shows nothing.
